quest.title: Lightcall Resonance
quest.description: In the Tunigi Hollow, you, Paimon, and Sorush encounter an eccentric Pari. She seems to be preparing for some sort of trial...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x200, Primogem x30, Mora x15000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Ah la la, ah la la~ Harder, farther, with more twists and turns. It will surely scare away all the goons~

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Oh? Isn't this Jarjar? Even after all these years, you're still stuck in your own little world.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Ah la? You're... Lady Sorush?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Do you know this Pari?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I've met her once a long time ago. We're not that familiar, but I've heard stories about her.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Besides, Jarjar's eccentric character is well known among the Pari.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: She always uses these things from who knows where, and messes around building nonsensical "challenges"... Most of the Pari try to avoid her.

choices.text: I don't know what to make of this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Sorush, are you sure it's okay to be judging someone to her face?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You don't know her all that well, right? So maybe you shouldn't believe everything you heard. What if she's changed now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And she looks pretty enthusiastic... Maybe she's doing something good for the Pari!

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Ah la la, no worries. After all, Lady Sorush is held in high regard by Lady Zurvan and shoulders great responsibilities.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Perhaps Lady Sorush will one day be as famous as the divine bird Simurgh. To turn one's nose up at a random nobody such as myself is but a given.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: The fact that Lady Sorush has anything at all to say about me is already an honor.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Whoa! That's... that's all in the past now. Let bygones be bygones!

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: B—But... we Pari should remember the happenings of the past...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Ahem! In the past, I distanced myself from my fellow Pari and took the wrong... no, the longer path! But that's enough about me. Tell me more about you!

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Ah la la, as you can see, I'm preparing something called "Lightcall Resonance" so I can fend off those Skeptic goons.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: They approached me with the pretense of wanting to be friends and drilled me with questions, trying to get things out of me that no human can learn. They've been getting on my nerves...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why would the Order of Skeptics even do that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe they're Nasejuna's minions. After all, Sorush has been tricked by him before.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: I don't know who you're talking about, but whoever they are, it won't matter. The Lightcall Resonance will drive them all out.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: I've made it clear to them that anyone who fails to pass the Lightcall Resonance is too stupid and weak to ask me questions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From what Paimon gathered, this Lightcall Resonance thing sounds like some kind of trial.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is it a test of fighting ability? Or a test of speed?

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Ah la la, it's the latter. That was quick! You guys really know your stuff.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Collecting certain items in a limited time and getting to the finish line as quickly as possible... This is a form of trial that humans are most familiar with.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Are you interested? Oh, I know! Why don't you try it out?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #No way! {NICKNAME} is my Yasnapati. You can't just casually ask us to help you!

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: #It's exactly because {M#he}{F#she} has the honor of being Lady Sorush's Yasnapati that it's got to be {M#him}{F#her}.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: #The Yasnapati of Lady Sorush is also well renowned among the humans. For Lightcall Resonance to meet with {M#his}{F#her} approval would be the highest honor.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: If Lightcall Resonance ever becomes an important rite for selecting courageous humans, Lady Sorush should deserve all the credit for having made it happen.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Just a few moments from you and your Yasnapati will bring your name glory. Wouldn't that be nice?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Is that so...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #Ahem! Of course! I just didn't... didn't want {NICKNAME} to go running around for nothing!

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: #The Order of Skeptics goons have offered me some nice things. They're of no use to me and I'd happily give them to the Yasnapati and {M#his}{F#her} Pale Floater as a reward.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nice things! Rewards for Paimon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: See, Sorush? What more can be said? Let's go and help Jarjar!

choices.text: It's just a speed challenge anyway...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Can't say I really care about the rewards.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But since you're interested... Just say yes to Jarjar, and make it quick!

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Ah la la, how decisive! It looks like great Sorush's Yasnapati has a lot of experience and confidence.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: This is the first, simplest test of Lightcall Resonance. Let's begin whenever you're ready.

choices.text: It's gonna be a piece of cake.

talks.objective: Talk to Jarjar and start the trial

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm ready!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah! We're no scrubs, and we always do our best!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #It's just a test to hold back the Order of Skeptics. It'll be a walk in the park for me and {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Ah la la! Wonderful! You sound so confident.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Show me your moves!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Ah la la, as expected of Lady Sorush and her Yasnapati. You made it through with ease!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: But be warned, that was just the beginning...

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I still have to adjust the layout of the second trial. Please wait until the next day and find me at the next location. Let me give you a rough estimate of where that'll be...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You need a whole day for that? Are you planning to bump the difficulty up after seeing how strong we are?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #No matter. Jarjar isn't aware of what {NICKNAME} is truly capable of. {M#He}{F#She}'s able to handle anything no matter how difficult it gets.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Ah la la, you're here.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I didn't get the chance to ask you yesterday, but how did the first trial feel?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Easy peasy, lemon squeezy!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmph! If all you want is to stop those Skeptics from bothering you, just make your trial as difficult as possible so that no one passes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As long as you give them a hard time from the get-go, no one would ever dare mess with you again!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Jarjar?

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Ah la, it's nothing. Let's continue.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: You know the rules! Collect all the particles and reach the end as fast as you can.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh, never mind. We're only here to help a little Pari evaluate the effectiveness of her trials and get our rewards when we're done, that's it!

talks.objective: Talk to Jarjar and start the trial

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bring the Pari trial on!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! That sounds kinda strange... but Paimon understands what you mean! Hehe, you wouldn't want to miss our performance, Jarjar!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and Pale Floater are really energetic... Maybe I should be a little more proactive too.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I—Impressive! You got through the second trial without breaking a sweat... It was supposed to be much more complex than the first!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Was I not strict enough with the rules? Should I cut down the time limit...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jarjar looks like she's getting serious. Maybe we've stirred up her competitive spirit!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Could be. Looks like she's thinking about the details of the trial...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Is it just her competitive spirit?)

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Irrelevant topics aside, the challenge is still not over...

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: As is customary, I need some time to prepare for the next trial. Please wait until tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Ah la, you guys held up your end of the bargain.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Now, let's discuss the details of the last trial. For example, did you find the difference in height between each track too repetitive, or were the obstacles too sparse...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: There she goes again, rambling with words no Pari would ever use. Do we really have to talk about such trifling matters before a trial?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I don't need to be part of this conversation about nitty gritty details. You can talk amongst yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: When you're just about ready, come call for me.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: #It looks like that last trial wasn't challenging enough for you, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I thought about your suggestions, and I think it's indeed necessary to make a few modifications and make Lightcall Resonance more fearsome...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why don't you call me "Lady Sorush's Yasnapati" anymore?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, yeah! Now that Paimon thinks about it, all the "ah la la's" in her speech are gone, and she sounds more concise! She really should speak like this more often.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: When you were talking earlier, you kinda sounded like the Skeptics. It was as if you were... putting on airs, and you were way too reverent towards Sorush... Aren't you supposed to hate the Skeptics?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and we forgot to ask, but what did the Order of Skeptics want from you...?

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Wow... how perceptive of you.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Well, I guess there's no point hiding it from you... Hmm, where should I start?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I knew something was up.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! What's the big idea? Paimon's falling behind!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: No worries, innocent Pale Floater. It's better not to know these things, as the more you know, the more troublesome it gets.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: #You seem to like treasure and seem solely focused on whether the rewards will make you happy. I'll let {NICKNAME} deal with all the heavy emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #No way! Paimon would never let {NICKNAME} be unhappy alone! Paimon's gonna listen to you talk!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Is this what they call true friendship? What have I been doing... except making a fool of myself...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What?

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Alright, enough prattling, back to business. Come and try another round of Lightcall Resonance. This is no ordinary trial, and you may not make it through this time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay, we'll talk later after taking on your painstakingly prepared challenge...

talks.objective: Talk to Jarjar and start the trial

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's get started.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Something feels off... Did Paimon miss an important conversation?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's wait. I want to start later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Are you tired? Do you wanna eat something to recover your strength?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} has always been rather cautious with {M#his}{F#her} actions. I'm sure {M#he}{F#she} has some considerations of {M#his}{F#her} own.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I see... Feel free to get everything in order before proceeding. I'll be right here waiting for you!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I've never seen anything like this... Ohh, you must be the ones I've been waiting for... But you're also Lady Sorush's Yasnapati...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm? Jarjar, you don't look too happy.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: What happened? What's Jarjar muttering now?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: This Lightcall Resonance trial was quite a struggle. I'm a little tired... so I didn't quite catch that.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: It's nothing! Let's focus on the trial...

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Lady Sorush seems to be tired, and I also have to prepare the final track... I'll see you when it's done, as usual. Then we can chat again.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: That's very sensible of you. Good, I'll take a short break.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: My Yasnapati, next time you meet Jarjar, go on and chat without me. I'll be nearby having a rest and recuperating my strength...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: This will give you time to chat about the trivial issues that you discussed earlier.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Uh... oh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry, Sorush! When the time comes, we'll give Jarjar some feedback!

choices.text: (Give Paimon a hint with your eyes.)

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: With the way you're carrying yourselves, do you really think you can pull this one off?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Of course. Like you said, {NICKNAME} is Lady Sorush's Yasnapati. {M#He}{F#She} eats these challenges for breakfast!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell us the truth, first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Jarjar! Anything you're not telling us and Sorush, spit it out.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: It's really no big deal. A solitary Pari, tricked by people with ulterior motives. Nothing more.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I was originally fond of flying freely in pursuit of speed and skill, and arranged many challenges similar to Lightcall Resonance. But no Pari wanted to enjoy them with me.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: An Order of Skeptics goon appeared and said he wanted to be my friend.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: It was obvious that no matter which wind glider he used, he proved to be an amateur. And yet, I fell for his sycophantic overtures.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: In the end, he saw me as nothing more than an observational sample of ordinary Pari to be used... He also tried to get information about an important Pari out from me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: An important Pari... It must be Zurvan.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: That's right. Compared with the first Pari, the great Lady Zurvan, I'm but a lowly, nameless Pari that no one cares about.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: The humans treat me well, but not because of who I am, but because of the information I know.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sounds familiar...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, Sorush was cheated for the exact same reason.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I may be a simple nameless Pari, but I don't give away secrets easily. When I found out the truth, I drove him away.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I thought that would be the end of it, but then another human came into contact with me, as if unaware that I had just chased his companion away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are these people all working under Nasejuna? To think that he would do all these things, in addition to tricking Sorush!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How demeaning.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: This is why I came up with Lightcall Resonance. I wanted to show the humans that only those who have passed the trials have the right to speak to me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What about those who pass the trials?

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I will never tell them a single thing about Lady Zurvan even if they do pass the trials. This is a matter of principles.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Lady Sorush is right. I'm a strange Pari, always alone...

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: But I won't ever sell out any Pari for the sake of being friends with humans.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that sounds harsh!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorush's situation isn't quite the same.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true... But anyway, you wanna make more friends, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #It seems a little weird to say it right now, but didn't {NICKNAME} pass all the trials? {M#He}{F#She} could be your friend.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: #No. {NICKNAME} is your friend and Sorush's Yasnapati. How could I...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Friendships aren't like those strange one-on-one master-servant relationships!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can be friends with Paimon and Sorush, that's all there is to it! Let everyone try out your gliding challenge, enjoy your Lightcall Resonance, and be happy!

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: You... you...

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: The treasure. You can have it now. I don't know how else to express my gratitude... And as for Sorush... never mind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Jarjar chickened out at the most crucial moment... That won't do!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's obvious that you're still talking to Sorush like a member of the Order of Skeptics. What do you think of her?

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: No way! Sorush is such a special Pari. Her resolve and willpower is something I could never hope to learn. I have a lot of respect for her.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: I just thought that if the Order of Skeptics's manner of speaking could please me to the point where I let my guard down, it must be good enough to make other Pari feel happy too. I thought that it'll make them more willing to talk to me...

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Come to think of it, perhaps I should stop imitating this manner of flattery. I should be friends with Sorush as my true self...

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: But I'm a little scared... If I don't praise Sorush enough, she'll remember the rumors and won't want anything to do with me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That won't happen. How should Paimon put it? Sorush is a totally different Pari now! She was willing to talk to you from the beginning, wasn't she?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And since you already have a high regard for her, Paimon's sure she'll feel your respect — even if you don't use the Order of Skeptics's manner of talking!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! There's no going back now, and the treasure isn't important anymore. If we pass this final trial of Lightcall Resonance, you have to try to become friends with Sorush.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Otherwise, when {NICKNAME} and Paimon travel somewhere else, you'll go back to being lonely and miserable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, at least until the next time someone passes Lightcall Resonance... but Paimon has no idea when that'll be.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Hey... don't be so sure of your success! This last trial will be a challenging one!

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Let's wait until you complete the trial before crossing that troublesome bridge...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph! We won't be underestimated! We've got this final challenge in the bag!

choices.text: If we pass the trial, you should give it a try.

talks.objective: Talk to Jarjar and start the trial

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's go. We'll get through it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we succeed, you have to make good on your promise and tell Sorush how you really feel!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Uh... okay. I'll do my best!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: The difficulty has been ratcheted up this time, so don't be careless! Are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Just so you know, compared to the last two, this trial will definitely be challenging for you. If you don't give it your all, you might get knocked down!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Okay, now all of Jarjar's trials are complete.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The last trial did feel a little more complex. It took us quite some time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your turn, Jarjar. Just go ahead and cut to the chase!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Ah la la, Lady Sorush. Of course Lightcall Resonance would be slightly difficult. How would you have bothered your Yasnapati to come and have a look otherwise?

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: If it ended too soon, Lightcall Resonance wouldn't deserve to become a proper testing ritual — and it would've been a waste of your precious time. I hope you understand!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Fair point... I'll let the matter go, then.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Jarjar, what's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's with that tone? What happened to showing who you really are?

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I can't help it! I'm not ready. I can't even get the words out!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I can't just tell Sorush that I've been copying the Skeptics' manner of speech... She'll get really mad, that's for sure. Even the thought of it is terrifying!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: What are you muttering about?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Anyway, my Yasnapati, what do you think about Jarjar's Lightcall Resonance?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #Then I guess there really is something special about it, since even {NICKNAME} says so.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmm, surely it wouldn't be a bad thing to spend more time with her.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Ahem! You may consider me your most distinguished friend, Jarjar. Not many among the Pari are that lucky.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: ...Friend?

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: If... if I built a more powerful trial than Lightcall Resonance, would you consider... giving it a try yourself?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: That's hard to say! I have a busy schedule, you know?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ...However, on the rare occasion when time permits, I'll think about it.

response.speaker: Jarjar
response.text: Thank you so very much, Lady Sorush! I... I... I promise I'll do my bestest to create the most satisfactory trial for you!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Why the sudden excitement? You... still have a lot to learn about how to socialize with the other Pari!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Should we say that, thanks to Sorush's insensitivity, Jarjar's problem has been inadvertently solved?

choices.text: At least... it's a good ending.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! I hope they get along from now on!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, the Lightcall Resonance trial was just right for someone as tall as you, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But don't you think Sorush is a little too small for the trial? Paimon can just imagine her stomping her feet in anger when she fails!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: The trial has begun. Let's chat when you're finished, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Or perhaps, you'd like to begin a little later?

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: As expected of you!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: What do you think? Is there anything else that needs preparing?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, since you said so, I'll take my time to get ready.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ohhhhh! Is {NICKNAME} getting serious?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #You can't go wrong with a little caution. It's totally {NICKNAME}'s style.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That sounds terrifying! I need to prepare some more!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? You're just playing along, right? Paimon feels like you're exaggerating things...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But it's probably for the best to make sure you put your best foot forward.

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: I mean it this time! For this final trial, I've come up with the hardest setup I can think of, so you'd better give it your all...

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Ahem! I mean... get ready to fail!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let me make some adjustments.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, let's get serious about getting Jarjar and Sorush to be friends!

dialogues.speaker: Jarjar
dialogues.text: Didn't I tell you not to get your hopes up!?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You return to Jarjar's side.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You return to Jarjar's side together with Sorush, who is still unaware of the situation...
